The crew of the Royal Mail liner Arlanza, which was due to sail to Buenos Aires from Southampton on September 4, refused to day to accept the wage reduction and left the Board of Trade Office without signing on.
On the other hand the captain of the “transport Derbyshire which opens the autumn trooping season on Wednesday by taking reliefs to India said he had obtained practically a full crew.

label: text
text: The decision of the "Strike Council to attend the compulsory conference of all unions summoned by the President of the Arbitration Court has aroused hopes that the strike will soon end.

label: text
text:
Bombay, August 31.
The first batch of Indian Lascars numbering 700 has been recruited for service in connection with the shipping strike. They are proceeding to South Africa shortly. More are expected to snill later.

label: text
text: A meeting of seamen at Avonmouth passed a resolution stating their intention to hold up the New Zealand liner Piako, due to sail on Wednesday, until the wages reduction has been restored.

label: text
text: The secretary of the Amalgamated Marine Workers' Union, the rival to the Sailors and Firemen's Union, stated to-day that his union was not officially backing the seamen's strike.

label: text
text: He claimed to be responsible for the Arlanzás crew refusing to sign on. He declared that the crew of the White Star liner Majestic, who signed on last week, had decided to go: 24 hours' notice to terminate their articles. The men on the trooper Glamorganshire had also refused to sign on.

label: text
text: The Secretary of the Sailors and Firemen's Union declared the trouble at Southampton had been engineered by another union with small membership which was trying to get a new lease of life.

label: text
text:
A meeting of Hull seamen tonight, after hearing an official of the Marine Workers' Union, decided to join the strike. A committee was formed and pickets were detailed to visit the docks.
The meeting represented only a portion the seamen at Hull

label: text
text: Important developments are likely to result from the secret conference at Sydney last week-end between the labour leaders and the trade-unionists. It is understood that labour is endeavouring to settle the strike preferring to fight the deportation issue in connection with which there is talk of a federal election.

label: text
text: A leading member of the Cabinet is of the opinion that an election will be held in a few months. Several applications have already been made to the Government to join the special police although the bill has not yet been approved by the Senate which passed it on a second reading after a strenuous debate. Summonses have been served requesting Messrs. Walsh and Johannsen to appear before the deportation board on September 3. —Reuter.

label: text
text: The shipping strike has extended and five vessels are now affected. —Reuter.

label: text
text:
Johannesburg, August 31.
The Transvaal labour conference has passed a resolution recognising the justice of the semmen's strike and calling on the Government to refuse to support the shipping companies against the strikers. Colonel Cresswell, the labour minister, opposing the resolution, deprecated the notion of the men refusing to carry out the agreements centered into by their unions.—Reuter.

text: The report_from Jerusalem that Jebel Druses have captured the citadel of Sueida is discredited at the Quii d'Orsay.

label: text
text: General Sarrail, telegraphing yesterday, says as a reprisal for minor losses snipers inflicted on the French garrison at the citadel, thirty French aeroplanes bombed the Druse quarters at Sueida. He does not mention the fall of the citadel.

label: text
text: A telegram from Beyrout enies the reported fall of Sueida and adds that all is quiet.

label: text
text: The submarine Veier6 has not returned to the base from the naval manoeuvres. Aeroplanes, destroyers and submarities are searching for the Venero by day and night. The ships are using the hydrophonic apparatus.

A correspondent signing himself “Philosopher”, writes to the “North China Daily News” as follows:—
Sir,—'The news in your issue of 10-day, that residents of Hongkong have met and passed a resolution to cable Home asking that firm action be taken against Canton, must give great satisfaction to all foreigners in China.

label: text
text: Would it be possible for foreign communities in other large centres to do likewise?

label: text
text: If the different nationals in Shanghai and other important centres had similar meetings, and each meeting sent cabled representations to its own Home Government, the present disturbed conditions throughout China would end the sooner.

label: text
text: I believe most foreigners realize that they must make common cause and employ their joint resources against a people who mistake elemeney for weakness, and who, in spite of their many good qualities, are more corrupt in private and in public life than any other nation which is thought to be civilized.

label: text
text: In order to decide who are Far East Creditors the interested parties should submit proof that they came under one, or other of the categories above mentioned on 26th July, 1921.

label: text
text: The bonds offered to the Far Eastern creditors are of 50 G.$ U.S.A. and bearing interest at 50 per cent. payable half-yearly, that is to say G.$ 1.25 on the 15th January and G.$ 1.25 on the 15th July of every year. The first coupon due on 15th July will be paid on delivery of the bonds.

label: text
text: The bonds are redeemable in 23 years by drawings taking place on the 1st December of every year.

label: text
text: the 1st December of every year, reimbursements being effected on the 15th January following. The first drawing will take place on 1st December, 1925.

label: text
text: Payment of coupons due and reimbursement of drawn bonds will be effected:

label: text
text: (a) In New York in U.S.A. Gold Dollars at a place to be designated by the Société Française de Gérance de la Banque Industrielle de Chine (Franco-Chinese Institution).

label: text
text: (b) In Peking, Shanghai and Saigon at the offices of the S.F.G. etc., and in all other places which may be designated by this Company in local currency at the rate of exchange at Sight on New York on the day of presentation.

label: text
text: Annual payments which are to assure the service of the interest and amortization of these bonds are secured on the revenues of the Chinese Maritime Customs and on those of the Native Customs administered by the Chinese Maritime Customs in the open Ports and eventually on the revenues of the Salt Gabelle.

label: text
text: These Gold $ Bonds are signed by the Inspector General of the Chinese Maritime Customs who is charged, as is well known, with the centralisation and distribution of both the Maritime and Native Customs.

label: text
text: The Far Eastern creditors of the B.I.C. have already some months ago been asked individually to make it known if they wished to receive Gold dollar Bonds instead of Repartition Bonds, an option which is reserved to them by Art. 8 of the Transactional Settlement. Those who have not yet replied and who wish to get G&B Bonds ARE REQUESTED TO MAKE IT KNOWN AS SOON AS POSSIBLE AND IN ANY CASE BEFORE 31st October.
